stem: (Select TWO.) Dunmore Analytics' newest engineer is walking through two claims a teammate made about how a `data` block and a `terraform_data` resource actually behave day to day. Which two of the following statements are correct?

choices.text: A `terraform_data` resource is a `resource` block that stores a value under the managed-resource lifecycle without creating any real infrastructure
A data block always creates a placeholder object in the state file that stays there until a `terraform destroy` clears it out
Terraform re-reads a data source's value on every ordinary run, rather than caching it permanently after the first read
A data block appears in plan output as an add, change, or destroy action once Terraform reaches the apply step, the same as a resource block
A `terraform_data` resource can only be declared alongside another managed resource of the same type; it cannot stand on its own in a configuration

rationale: A `terraform_data` resource is a `resource` block that stores a value under the managed-resource lifecycle without creating real infrastructure -- exactly the exception this objective tests. Terraform re-reads an ordinary data source's value on every run rather than caching it once, so nothing about a data block's value is permanently locked after its first read. A data block's presence in state only records what it read; it is never a lasting placeholder object the way a resource's state entry is. A data block also never appears in plan output as an add, change, or destroy action, only as a read. And a `terraform_data` resource needs no other managed resource to attach to -- it exists precisely for cases with no other logical resource to hold the value.
